messages:
alex: heads up — customer CS-7845 reporting sustained 503s from hosted inference since ~10:12 UTC. curl to /v1/generate returns 503 and gateway timeouts. Happening across multiple regions for that tenant. sample: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` -> 503. Can we triage? :rotating_light:

maria: I'm seeing spike in upstream worker restarts on pool-gpu-3 around that time. kubectl get pods shows a restart loop on inference-worker-xyz. Logs show segfaults and occasional GPU OOM messages. grabbing logs now.

raj: paste from pod logs: ```
2026-02-21T10:11:57Z runtime ERROR: upstream worker crashed (exit signal 11)
2026-02-21T10:11:57Z runtime INFO: restarting container
2026-02-21T10:11:58Z gpu-manager WARN: GPU 0: out of memory while allocating 124 MiB
2026-02-21T10:11:58Z kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU lockup - resetting
```

jessie: customer says this started right after they switched to an 8k-context model variant yesterday. they included payload size + concurrency: 2 concurrent streams, prompt ~6k tokens, sampling set to top_k=40.

infra-bot: note — kube events on node ip-10-2-7-34: Kubelet has reported container exits; kernel dmesg lines include `out_of_memory` and `oom_kill` on cgroup: containerd://... Also recent node upgrade: nvidia-driver 525.85 -> 525.90 applied at 09:45 UTC.

maria: reproducing locally on staging: I forced similar input and saw the same segfault within ~30s. nvidia-smi snapshot from the pod: ```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.90.03    Driver Version: 525.90.03    CUDA Version: 12.1   |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. |
| 0    A100-SXM4...      On      | 00000000:65:00.0 Off |                  0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory Usage         |
|    0  12537  C      python                          49927MiB / 81920MiB     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

raj: two hypotheses: (1) actual GPU OOM from model+batch combined with a driver-level race causing SIGSEGV on alloc path; (2) memory leak in KV cache for this model variant (new 8k token path). We have a recent runtime change that altered prefetch logic last week.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation steps: 1) cordon node ip-10-2-7-34, 2) drain pods from that node to avoid customer impact, 3) scale up pool-gpu to give headroom, 4) create a temporary routing rule to divert tenant CS-7845 to dedicated pool with smaller batch caps. Doing 1-3 now.

maria: done cordon + drain. rerouted CS-7845 to pool-gpu-5 (older driver 525.85). errors dropped for that tenant immediately. other tenants still seeing occasional 503s correlated to same node.

raj: collect artifacts for root cause: please capture pod coredump (if any), `dmesg` of node, `journalctl -u kubelet`, `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`, and runtime debug logs with trace-level for allocation. Also enable `--collect-kv-stats` on a debug rollout for one worker. Steps to collect: ```
# on node
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-1923456789.log
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b > /tmp/kubelet.log
kubectl cp $(kubectl get po -l app=inference -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'):/tmp/runtime.log ./runtime.log
sudo coredumpctl dump --output=/tmp/coredump-$(date +%s).core
```

jessie: I've opened an official customer incident and communicated the temporary routing and apology. They're ok with the mitigation but want ETA for permanent fix.

infra-bot: checking node upgrade history — cluster image pipeline rolled nvidia-driver 525.90.03 to a subset of GPU nodes yesterday as part of driver-ramp. Rollout window 09:30-09:50 UTC. 525.90 release notes mention fixes but also a known regression on allocation path for some A100 kernels (internal QA flagged flaky).

raj: okay that's a smoking gun. Plan: rollback driver on affected node set to 525.85 and pause the rest of the driver ramp. Need infra approval to rollback and run runtime+model smoke tests. Also propose a runtime guard: if allocation fails with SIGSEGV near driver reset, fallback to smaller batch and requeue request to different node instead of crashing. I'll open a PR after we confirm repro.

maria: TEL: rolling back drivers on the 3 affected nodes now. I've also disabled the prefetch debug flag we shipped last week and will push a canary with easier memory caps.

sre-oncall: monitoring — setting alert to suppress noisy restarts and instead surface unique regression metric: upstream-worker-exit-rate > 5 in 5m triggers pager. Also adding a mitigation playbook snippet to runbook: `/runbooks/gpu-upstream-crash.md` (internal).

raj: repro notes for engineering: high-token prompts + top_k sampling + concurrent streams appears to push KV allocations over threshold on the buggy driver. Repro script: ```
# reproduce load on staging
python tools/bench/generate_batch.py --model rdx-8k --prompt-size 6000 --concurrency 2 --top_k 40
```

maria: artifacts uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1923456789/{dmesg,kubelet,core,runtime.log}. Link shared in the incident ticket.

jessie: customer FYI: shared that we've routed traffic, rolled back drivers on affected nodes, and that we're actively working on a fix. They requested weekly updates until resolved.

raj: next action items: (A) infra: rollback driver rollout and block further 525.90 ramp (assigned to infra team), (B) eng-runtime: add defensive fallback + guard and postmortem (assigned to raj), (C) QA: run long-context stress tests across driver versions (assigned to maria). I'll coordinate PRs.

maria: current status — customer errors down to normal, node restarts stopped after rollback. leaving cordon in place until we've validated full stability. Will uncordon tomorrow if green.

sre-oncall: closing temporary incident channel here and creating a formal sev2 incident doc in incidents/ with timeline. tagging: @infra @eng-runtime @support to follow up. :white_check_mark:
